newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan cotton rates ease on funds shortage.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan cotton rates ease on funds shortage.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates closed lower on Tuesday as textile mills faced a shortage of funds needed to buy cotton from ginners, dealers said.
Dealer Abdul Qadir Kashan at the private Karachi Cotton Association (KCA) said banks had delayed releasing funds to mills, which had set off bearish sentiment and depressed prices.
Trading activity was dull as most mills had no cash to make prompt payments, Kashan said.
In the kerb market, the rate for NIAB-78 variety fluctuated between 2,375 and 2,410 rupees per maund (37.32 kg), the dealer said. Rates were likely to open lower on Wednesday.
